name: Ola
summary: Candidates commonly report that Ola's engineering interviews include a coding test, problem-solving rounds, a design round and a hiring manager conversation, with design problems often drawn from ride-hailing: matching riders and drivers, pricing, arrival times and maps. Ola's careers page describes traits such as 'Impact oriented', 'Ambitious Goals' and 'Obsessively hyperlocal'. Ola Electric is a separate company that hires for its own teams, such as R&D, design and manufacturing; this guide focuses on mobility.
rounds: Online coding test (for many engineering roles)
Low-level or system design round, often on a mobility problem
looks_for: Designing real-time systems that work across a whole city
Caring about driver partners as well as riders

questions.text: Tell me about a project where you set an ambitious goal. How close did you get?
covers: The goal and why it was ambitious
What you did differently to reach for it
How close you got, and what you learned from the gap

questions.text: Describe a time you solved a problem that was specific to one city, area or group of users.
covers: What made that place or group different
How you learned about it: data, visits, talking to users
The local fix and its result

questions.text: Tell me about a time you tried something new without a clear playbook to follow.
covers: Why there was no playbook
How you set up a small experiment and judged it
What you kept, dropped or scaled

questions.text: Tell me about a launch that didn't go as planned. What did you do in the first few hours?
covers: What went wrong and how you found out
Your first steps: limiting the damage, telling people
What you changed in how you launch since

questions.text: How would you design the system that matches a ride request to a nearby driver?
covers: Live driver locations in a geo index, such as geohash cells
Choosing a driver by pickup time, likelihood of accepting and fairness
Never offering one driver two rides at once, plus timeouts and re-matching

questions.text: How would you design pricing for rides when demand rises sharply, such as in heavy rain?
covers: Measuring demand and supply per small area, minute by minute
Price rules with caps, shown clearly to riders before they book
The effect on drivers coming online, and how you'd test changes safely

questions.text: How would you store and query driver locations that update every few seconds?
covers: An in-memory store, with old locations expiring
Handling heavy write traffic: splitting by city or region
Fast nearby searches, and what to do with stale points

questions.text: How would you calculate the fare for an auto ride when GPS drops out halfway through the trip?
covers: Detecting gaps, and snapping points to the road
Estimating the missing stretch from the likely route
Being fair to both rider and driver, and handling disputes

questions.text: Riders in one city say drivers cancel after accepting. How would you investigate and reduce it?
covers: Splitting cancellations by area, time, pickup distance and trip type
The driver's side: pickup too far, destination, payment method, earnings
A fix tested in part of the city, with cancellation rate and wait time as metrics

questions.text: How would you make a ride app work reliably when the network drops in and out during a trip?
covers: Keeping trip state on the phone and syncing when back online
Safe retries so actions such as ending a trip happen once
Battery and data use, and resolving conflicts between phone and server

questions.text: How would you increase the number of drivers available in one part of a city during the morning peak?
covers: Finding the gap: where, when and how big
Options: targeted incentives, earnings-per-hour support, showing drivers where demand is
Cost per extra ride and whether drivers keep coming after incentives end

questions.text: How would you design over-the-air software updates for connected vehicles so a bad update can't leave riders stranded?
covers: Signed updates and a staged rollout to a small group first
Installing only when safe, such as parked with enough battery
Keeping the old version to fall back to, and monitoring after each stage

questions.text: Why Ola? Which part of its business interests you most?
covers: A specific area, such as rides, maps or payments, and why
What you know about its riders and drivers
How your skills fit

questions.text: Why do you want to build products for Indian cities, and which local problem would you most like to solve?
covers: A specific problem you've seen yourself
Why it's hard and who it affects
How you'd start working on it

tips: Expect design topics from ride-hailing (matching, pricing, arrival times, maps); practise one end to end with rough numbers.
Bring the driver partner into your answers: earnings, cancellations and how the app treats them decide how many drivers are online.
Ola's careers page stresses being hyperlocal; examples about specific cities, areas or traffic patterns make answers concrete.
Applying to Ola Electric? Check its own careers page for the team you want; its teams (R&D, design, manufacturing, supply chain) need domain preparation.
